cars.generation: Original BMW Technik composite-bodied front-mid-engine roadster
cars.specification_market: BMW June 6, 2012 engineering retrospective: production roadster first delivered early 1989, distinct from 1986 development study and 1987 show reveal. Engine class remains nominal 2.5 litres; ambiguous historical hp convention, unsourced exact cc, Alpina conversions, Art Car paint, prototypes and later Z3/Z4 specifications are omitted.
cars.summary: The Z1 turned BMW Technik research into an unusually innovative production sports car: vertically retracting doors, replaceable plastic outer panels, a bonded composite floor and the new multi-link Z-axle. Its front-mid-engine layout and manual transmission made the experimental construction part of a coherent driver-focused roadster, establishing the modern BMW Z-car line.

cars.specification_market: Factory archive 121.042 roadster data, original May 1955 main-series reference. Exact swept volume 1897 cc is separate from 1882-cc tax classification. Original 8.5 compression and unboosted hydraulic brakes are separate from September 1959 compression, May 1956 booster, 1960 weight and August 1961 engine changes. Alternate gearbox/final-drive ratios, hardtop coupe, prototype and light-door sports accessory specification are excluded.
cars.summary: The 190 SL established the elegant open touring side of the Mercedes-Benz SL tradition alongside the competition-derived 300 SL. Its recognisable roadster design, new overhead-cam four-cylinder engine and independently suspended Ponton-based chassis made it a foundational sporting grand tourer with lasting historical significance.
